newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slump but seen rebounding next week.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slump but seen rebounding next week.

text.p: Danish share prices ended the week on a low note after Thursday's Wall Street decline but traders expected Copenhagen prices to rebound on Monday.

"The market has been very volatile of late so one could well expect a slight rise on Monday after today's fall," a dealer told Reuters, adding that some potential sellers had backed off on Friday whenever buying interest became serious.
The KFX top-20 index fell 1.25 point to 143.51 in overall bourse turnover of 1.193 billion crowns and its March future fell 2.05 point to 143.51 with 380 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Coloplast, SAS, Radiometer and A.P.Moeller's D/S Svendborg were the only top-20 shares to buck the downward trend.
Coloplast rose five crowns to 690 and SAS edged up 0.50 crown to 80.50 while Radiometer gained three crowns to 372.
Svendborg's b-share put on 1,000 crowns to close at 251,000 but its sister share, D/S 1912, went 2,000 crowns in the other direction, ending at 172,500 crowns.
Froday's star was non-KFX Aarhus Football Club which scored a 50-crown rise to 580 after selling defender Lennart Bak for five million crowns. --Morten Bonde Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +33969659
